unit.local_context: Standard 1-category theory lemma: pullback limits transport along a categorical equivalence. Second hand-authored reference example for formalization readiness.
unit.proof: Because F is an equivalence, it is fully faithful and admits a quasi-inverse G : D → C. Given a cone (Q, q₁, q₂) over (F f, F g) in D, apply G to obtain a cone over (f, g) in C. The universal property of the pullback (P, π₁, π₂) yields a unique mediating morphism u : GQ → P in C; applying F gives a mediating morphism F u : Q → F P in D. Uniqueness follows from full faithfulness of F. Essential surjectivity ensures that the transported pullback object is correct up to canonical isomorphism.
unit.statement: Let C and D be categories and F : C ≃ D an equivalence of categories. If a cospan (f : X → Z, g : Y → Z) admits a pullback (P, π₁, π₂) in C, then (F f, F g) admits a pullback (F P, F π₁, F π₂) in D, and F induces an equivalence between the categories of pullback cones over (f, g) and over (F f, F g).

unit.local_context: Classical finite graph theory theorem used as the first reference example.
unit.proof: We argue by induction on |V|. If |V|=1, then G has no edges. Otherwise, choose a leaf v, let G' = G - v, and apply the induction hypothesis to G'. Since v is a leaf, deleting v removes one vertex and one edge. Hence |E|-1 = (|V|-1)-1, so |E| = |V|-1.
unit.statement: Let G=(V,E) be a finite tree. Then |E| = |V| - 1.
